title: Man shot by Hamilton police dies; SIU now says he did not appear to shoot
subtitle: The SIU said it cannot currently confirm whether the man was armed.
article: A 43-year-old man has died after being shot by Hamilton police Saturday.

Around 5 p.m. Saturday, a resident of an apartment building at 1964 Main St. W. called police to report a man "acting in a threatening manner," Ontario's Special Investigations Unit said in a news release .

The SIU says Hamilton police officers made their way to the fifth floor of the building where they interacted with a "person of interest." Two officers discharged their guns, and one officer and the man were struck, according to the police watchdog.
Though the SIU initially described the incident as an "exchange of gunfire," the agency says it no longer appears that the man fired any shots at the officers.

In an earlier news release, the SIU said a police officer and a man in his 30s were injured in an exchange of gunfire. In a subsequent email to the Star, the SIU said it cannot currently confirm whether the man was armed.
On Monday, the agency added it recovered a replica firearm and the two officers' guns from the scene.
The officer and the man were both taken to hospital. The man, who sustained life-threatening injuries, was pronounced dead at 12:47 a.m. on Sunday.
The police officer has since been released from the hospital after receiving treatment for minor injuries, the SIU said.
The agency said it has assigned six investigators and two forensic investigators to the case and scheduled a post-mortem for Monday in Toronto.

Photos from the scene Saturday night - a three-tower apartment building complex on the westernmost edge of the old city of Hamilton - showed an area cordoned off by police tape and several armed officers on scene.

The SIU is an independent agency that investigates situations involving officials, including police officers, that may have resulted in death, serious injury, sexual assault or shots fired at a person.
The police watchdog is urging anyone with information, including video or photos, to contact the lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529 or online at https://siu.on.ca/en/appeals.php .
With files from Mike Pearson, Metroland
